paper_diagnosis: Methanol poisoning without typical diagnostic clues or standard antidotes
disease_label_per_paper: Early intentional methanol ingestion treated empirically with CRRT and enteral ethanol despite normal anion gap
presentation_summary: 43-year-old woman was brought to the ED drowsy but arousable after intentionally ingesting 200-250 mL of a solution containing 95% methanol and 5% ethanol, bought online and mixed with juice.
She also reported ingesting about 80 flunitrazepam 2 mg tablets, total about 160 mg, creating a competing central respiratory depression context.

She presented about 1.5 hours after ingestion with stable vital signs and GCS E4V5M6; initial VBG showed pH 7.296, pCO2 58 mmHg, bicarbonate 27.4 mmol/L, base excess +3.1 mmol/L, and anion gap 8.6 mmol/L.
Serum osmolality and serum methanol were unavailable at the treating facility, and urine methanol testing was not immediately available.
On ICU admission she developed respiratory acidosis, pH 7.187 and pCO2 71.1 mmHg, attributed to central hypoventilation from flunitrazepam co-ingestion rather than formate acidosis.
Because of the credible high-dose methanol ingestion history, she received early gastric aspiration, CRRT, enteral ethanol, and folinic acid before objective confirmation.
Retrospective admission urine testing confirmed methanol, while she remained without visual symptoms or neurologic deterioration and was transferred to psychiatric care on hospital day 3.

quality_warnings: This is an intentionally atypical early-presenting methanol case: normal anion gap, no metabolic acidosis, and no visual symptoms are encoded as true negative observations and not deleted.
The retrospective urine methanol result and estimated serum methanol are confirmatory, not available for presentation diagnosis, and are marked use_in_ranking:false.

The article contains a unit inconsistency for urine methanol: the case table renders mg/dL, while the discussion/table comparison and estimated serum calculation use mg/L. The JSON uses mg/L and records this warning.
Serum methanol and serum osmolality were unavailable at the treating facility; no numeric serum_methanol_concentration or serum_osmolality is invented.
The source reports initial pH/pCO2 as venous; these are encoded on shared blood-gas axes with specimen_type='venous_blood_gas'.
